questions.question: Infant mortality rate is the number of infants per thousand who die before reaching _______ year(s) of age.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**one**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Infant mortality rate refers to the number of deaths of infants under one year of age per 1,000 live births.
 
• It is a critical indicator used to measure the overall health of a population, particularly maternal and child health services.
 
• The calculation of infant mortality rate is based on data collected from hospitals, birth registries, and surveys.
 
• Factors affecting infant mortality include access to healthcare, maternal nutrition, and socioeconomic conditions.
 
• Globally, organizations like WHO, UNICEF, and national health departments monitor infant mortality rates as part of public health assessment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neonatal mortality rate:** Refers to the number of deaths of newborns within the first 28 days of life per 1,000 live births.
 
• **Postneonatal mortality rate:** Refers to the number of deaths of infants aged 29 days to one year per 1,000 live births.
 
• **Under-five mortality rate:** Refers to the number of deaths of children under five years of age per 1,000 live births.
 
• Countries with higher infant mortality rates often face challenges like poor healthcare infrastructure, malnutrition, and lack of sanitation.
 
• Reducing infant mortality is a key focus of international development goals, including the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goal 3 (Good Health and Well-Being).

questions.question: Which of the following animals is found in the Himalayan region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Snow Leopard**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Identification:** The **Snow Leopard** (*Panthera uncia*) is a large felid adapted to cold, mountainous environments; its thick coat, **long tail**, and stocky build distinguish it from lowland big cats.
 
• **Habitat & Altitude:** Found at high elevations in the **Himalayan** region, typically between about **3,000–5,500 metres**, inhabiting rocky ridges, alpine and subalpine zones.
 
• **Geographic Range in Himalayas:** Occurs across trans-Himalayan areas of **India** (e.g., Ladakh, parts of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim), **Nepal**, **Bhutan**, and adjacent ranges in **Pakistan** and western China.
 
• **Adaptations:** Features such as **dense fur**, wide nasal passages for cold air, large paws that act like snowshoes, and a **long, thick tail** for balance and warmth are specialised adaptations for alpine life.
 
• **Diet & Ecology:** Carnivorous predator feeding mainly on wild ungulates such as **bharal (blue sheep)**, Himalayan tahr and small mammals; typically **solitary** and crepuscular to nocturnal.
 
• **Conservation status:** Globally listed as **Vulnerable** (IUCN) with population concerns due to **poaching, habitat fragmentation**, and livestock–predator conflict.
 
• **Why other options are incorrect:** **Bengal Tiger** prefers **lowland forests and grasslands**; **Lion-tailed Macaque** is endemic to the **Western Ghats**; **Blackbuck** is a plains grassland antelope — none are alpine/Himalayan specialists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Distribution data:** The snow leopard’s range is discontinuous across high mountain systems; national populations are often estimated via **camera trapping** and **scat genetic analysis**.
 
• **Population estimates:** Global estimates are roughly around **4,000–6,500** individuals (estimates vary by source and survey year), highlighting the species’ **low density** even across vast ranges.
 
• **Legal protection:** In India the species receives strict protection under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** (Schedule I) and is listed in international conventions such as **CITES Appendix I**.
 
• **Threats & mitigation:** Major threats include **illegal trade**, decline of wild prey, and **retaliatory killings** for livestock depredation; mitigation includes community-based livestock management, compensation schemes, and protected area management.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Survey methods:** Reliable monitoring involves **camera traps**, spatial capture-recapture models, and **genetic analysis** of scat to estimate abundance.
 
• **Conservation actions:** Protected areas in the Himalaya, transboundary cooperation, and **community engagement** (e.g., predator-proof corrals, insurance/compensation) are critical for long-term survival.
 
• **Distinctiveness:** Remember that the snow leopard is a specialist of **cold, high-altitude ecosystems** — this ecological trait is the primary reason it is the correct answer for a Himalayan species question.

questions.question: The 'Chennai Port' is located along which of the following water bodies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bay of Bengal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chennai Port** is situated along the eastern coastline of India and faces the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• It is one of the oldest and largest ports in India, established in the year **1881**.
 
• Chennai Port is primarily used for handling bulk cargo, containers, automobiles, and petroleum products.
 
• The port plays a crucial role in India's maritime trade, serving as a gateway for exports and imports in the southern region of the country.
 
• Its strategic location on the Bay of Bengal provides easy connectivity to Southeast Asia and the Far East.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Bay of Bengal** is the northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, bounded by India and Sri Lanka to the west, Bangladesh to the north, and Myanmar and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to the east.
 
• It is the largest bay in the world, covering an area of around **2.2 million square kilometers**.
 
• The Bay of Bengal is known for its high biodiversity, including coral reefs, mangroves, and marine species like dolphins, turtles, and whales.
 
• Prominent rivers such as the Ganges, Brahmaputra, and Mahanadi drain into the Bay of Bengal, making it a hub for sediment deposition.
 
• The region is prone to cyclones due to its climatic conditions, with several major cyclones originating here annually.

questions.question: Which device is used to measure the current flow using needle deflection caused by a magnetic field force acting upon a current - carrying wire?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Galvanometer**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Galvanometer** is an instrument for detecting and measuring electric current by needle deflection.
 
• The deflection is caused by a magnetic field force acting upon a current-carrying wire within the device.
 
• It is a type of sensitive ammeter and can measure small currents accurately.
 
• Galvanometers are widely used in various applications including in analog meters and in the calibration of other instruments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Galvanometer** was named after Luigi Galvani, who discovered the principle of the device.
 
• It operates on the principle of electromagnetism, where an electric current creates a magnetic field.
 
• There are different types of galvanometers, including the moving coil and moving magnet types.
 
• Modern digital multimeters have largely replaced galvanometers for many applications but they are still used in specific scientific experiments and educational settings.

questions.question: Presence of which phenomenon leads to weakening of trade winds in a region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**El Nino.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **El Nino** is a phenomenon that leads to **weakening of trade winds** in a region.
 
• During El Nino, the** sea surface temperatures** in the Pacific Ocean near the Equator become **warmer **than usual, which affects the** atmospheric circulation **and leads to weakening of trade winds.
 
• Trade winds are the **prevailing easterly winds** that blow towards the **Equator in the tropics**, and they are important for **navigation and weather patterns.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coriolis force **is a phenomenon that influences the** direction of winds and ocean currents**, but it does not directly lead to weakening of trade winds.
 
• **Mango Shower** is a **meteorological phenomenon** that occurs in some parts of India during the **pre-monsoon season**, and it is not related to trade winds. 
 
• **La Nina** is a phenomenon that is opposite to **El Nino,** and it leads to **strengthening of trade winds** in a region.
 
• Hence, the statement "Presence of which phenomenon leads to weakening of trade winds in a region?" is **correctly answered** by option 3, El Nino.

questions.question: Which is the phase of the moon which is a full bright view of the moon, where the moon is almost perfect round in shape?

__
 
• The phase of the moon which is a full bright view of the moon, where the moon is almost perfect round in shape, is called the **Full moon**.
 
• In this phase, the entire face of the moon that is facing the Earth is illuminated by the Sun's light.
 
• The **Full moon** occurs approximately once every 29.5 days, which is the duration of a complete lunar cycle.
 
• This phase marks the midpoint of the lunar cycle, which starts with the New moon and progresses through the Waxing Crescent, First Quarter, Waxing Gibbous, Full moon, Waning Gibbous, Last Quarter, and Waning Crescent phases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **New moon** is the phase where the moon is not visible from Earth because the side of the moon that is illuminated by the Sun is facing away from Earth.
 
• The **Crescent moon** phases (Waxing and Waning) occur when only a small part of the moon is illuminated and visible from Earth.
 
• The **Gibbous moon** phases (Waxing and Waning) occur when more than half of the moon is illuminated but it is not yet a Full moon.
 
• The cycle of moon phases is caused by the relative positions of the Earth, Moon, and Sun. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/896a5352a810cf29d7293032fa61a1eb83d1264d436fc7bb053f0916431cae88.png]

questions.solution:

questions.question: Which article of the Constitution of India says that 'No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Article 21.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• Article21__

 __
 
• No one "shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty unless in accordance with a procedure established by law," according to Article 21. As a result, article 21 protects two rights: 1. The right to life, 2. The right to individual freedom.
 
• The Indian Constitution's Article 21 was established by the Government of India Act, 1935. It states that no one may be robbed of their life or personal freedom until doing so in accordance with the legal process. One of the essential freedoms that all Indian citizens are entitled to is Article 21, which is found in Part III of the Indian Constitution. Several rights and liberties that are a part of Article 21 will be covered in this article.
 
• Article 21A declares that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years. It is added by the 86th Constitution Amendment Act, 2002. 
 
• The right to life in Article 21 of Indian constitution does not mean animal existence or the mere act of breathing. It guarantees the right to a dignified life.
 
 
 
• History Judgements-
 
 
• Kharak Singh vs. the State of UP and Others: Right to privacy was included in Article 21 by this case.
 
• Sunil Batra vs. Delhi Administration: In this case, Supreme Court deemed the fatal handcuffs for the convicted persons as unconstitutional as it suggests inhuman behavior towards the prisoner. The court reiterated the clause “protection to the convicted and accused person” under Article 21.
 
• Mohini Jain vs. the State of Karnataka, 1992 SC: The SC held that the Right to life also includes the Right to education. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Article 21 of the Indian Constitution: Important Cases

 
 
• 1951's A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras In this case, the Supreme Court has applied a strict reading of Article 21. It was decided that only arbitrary executive activity is covered by Article 21's protection, not arbitrary legislative action. This indicates that a legislation may be used by the state to deny a person the rights guaranteed by Article 21.

questions.question: Life expectancy is an indicator of which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Human Development Report**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Life expectancy is a key indicator included in the **Human Development Index (HDI)**, which is part of the Human Development Report published annually by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• The Human Development Report aims to measure and rank countries based on human development indicators such as life expectancy, education, and income levels.
 
• Life expectancy reflects the average number of years a person is expected to live, based on current mortality rates.
 
• It is used to assess the health and well-being of populations globally and is influenced by factors such as healthcare quality, nutrition, and socio-economic conditions.
 
• The report helps policymakers design strategies to improve living standards and address inequalities in health, education, and income.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):**

 
 
• HDI is a composite index measuring a country's average achievements in three basic aspects of human development: health (life expectancy), education (mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling), and standard of living (gross national income per capita).
 
• It was introduced by the UNDP in 1990 as a measure of development beyond economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Life Expectancy:**
 
 
• Quality of healthcare services, access to medical facilities, and advancements in medical technology.
 
• Socio-economic factors, including poverty levels, education, and sanitation.
 
• Environmental factors, such as pollution levels and availability of clean water.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Life Expectancy:**
 
 
• It is a critical indicator of a country’s overall health infrastructure and development.
 
• Longer life expectancy often correlates with higher levels of socio-economic development and better living conditions.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends in Life Expectancy:**
 
 
• Life expectancy globally has increased due to advancements in healthcare, improved nutrition, and better living conditions.
 
• However, disparities exist between high-income and low-income countries due to unequal access to resources and healthcare.

questions.question: ________ is used to control the demand and supply of money.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Credit control.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Credit control** is used to control the** demand and supply of money.** 
 
• Credit control refers to the actions taken by the **central bank or monetary authority** to regulate the **availability and cost of credit** in the economy.
 
• By controlling the availability of credit, the central bank can influence the demand for money and therefore** control the money supply.**
 
• Credit control is important for maintaining **price stability and preventing inflation.**
 
• If the central bank allows too much credit to be available, it can lead to an **increase in demand for goods and services**, which can cause prices to rise.
 
• By controlling credit, the central bank can** prevent this** from happening.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One of the main tools used in credit control is the **setting of interest rates.**
 
• By increasing or decreasing interest rates, the central bank can make** credit more or less expensive**, which can influence the demand for money and the money supply.
 
• Other tools used in credit control include **reserve requirements, open market operations, and moral suasion.**
 
• **Reserve requirements** refer to the amount of money that banks are required to** hold in reserve, **which can influence the amount of credit they can lend.
 
• **Open market operations** involve the** buying and selling of government securities**, which can influence the amount of money in circulation.
 
• **Moral suasion **refers to the **use of persuasion and influence** to encourage banks to adopt certain policies or practices.
 
• **Equity control **refers to the **regulation of ownership** in companies and other assets. 
 
• It is not directly related to the **supply and demand of money.**

questions.question: The Mahayana Buddhism had two philosophical schools. Which of the following belonged to Mahayana Buddhism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhyamika and Yogachara.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Gautama Buddha** was born to Suddhodana (chief of republican Sakya clan) as Siddhartha in 563 BCE on Vaishakha Poornima day at Lumbini (Nepal).
 
• The** ultimate aim of the Buddha’s teachings** is the attainment of Nibbana/Nirvana.
 
• The philosophy of Buddha **accepts impermanence and transmigration **but denies the existence of God and believes that the soul is a myth.

**Mahayana School of Buddhism**-

 
• It literally means **“The Greater Path”.**
 
• The terms Hinayana & Mahayana were given by the Mahayana school.
 
• Mahayana has two main philosophical schools – the **Madhyamika & Yogachara. Hence option 1 is correct.**
 
• Its scriptures are in **Sanskrit.**
 
• This school of Buddhism considers **Buddha as God and worships idols of Buddhas & Bodhisattvas.**
 
• It believes in** universal liberation from sufferings** for all beings, and spiritual upliftment.
 
• **Salvation can also be attained **by means of faith and devotion to the mindfulness of the Buddha. It believes in mantras.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Madhyamaka **(The Middle Way School) and **Yogācāra **(The Meditative Practice School, also called Cittamātra [Mind Only] or Vijñanavāda (The Approach of Consciousness) are the two principal schools of **Mahāyāna Buddhist philosophy**.
 
• **Madhyamaka **is known for its doctrine of the ultimate emptiness and conventional reality of all phenomena, and for treating mind and external objects in parallel.
 
• **Yogācāra **is known for its apparent idealism, with a denial of the reality of the external world and an affirmation of the fundamental status of the mind or consciousness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Hinayana (Theravada) School of Buddhism**

 
• It literally means “**The Lesser path”** and Theravada signifies **“Doctrine of the Elders”.**
 
• Hinayana is true to the teachings of The Buddha.
 
• **Theravada** was the original school of Buddhist philosophy.
 
• Its scriptures are in** Pali.**
 
• **Doesn’t believe in idol worship.**
 
• Believes an individual can attain salvation through **self-discipline & meditation.**
 
• At present, it is found in Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, and other parts of South-East Asia.
 
• **Ashoka patronised Hinayana.**

**Vajrayana school of Buddhism-**

 
• It literally means **“Vehicle of Thunderbolt”.**
 
• The Vajrayana or “Diamond Vehicle” is also called **Mantrayana, Tantrayana, or Esoteric Buddhism.**
 
• It was established in Tibet in the 11th century.
 
• The **“Two Truth Doctrine”** is the central concept of Vajrayana. The two truths are identified as ‘**conventional’ & ‘ultimate’** truths. 
 
• Vajrayana texts use a highly symbolic language “**sandhya-bhasa” or “twilight language”. **
 
• Vajrayana **believes that salvation can be attained** by acquiring magical powers called **vajra.**
 
• It also lays importance on the** role of Buddhistavas** but favors fierce deities known as Taras.
 
• The rituals and devotion employ mantras (esoteric verbal formulas), mandalas (diagrams & painting for visualization practices), and a complex array of other rituals.
 
• It is predominant in Tibet, Nepal, Bhutan, and Mongolia.

questions.question: If x = 2 + √5, then the value of {( {x - (1)/(x)} )³} is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If x = √a + √b and a − b = 1, then 1/x = √a − √b.

Here x = √5 + 2, and (√5)² − 2² = 5 − 4 = 1.

⇒ 1/x = √5 − 2

⇒ x − 1/x = (√5 + 2) − (√5 − 2) = 4

⇒ (x − 1/x)³ = 4³ = 64

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x = 2 + √5

**To find:**

(x − 1/x)³

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1/x = 1 / (2 + √5)

To rationalize the denominator, multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate (2 − √5):

⇒ 1/x = (2 − √5) / [(2 + √5)(2 − √5)]

Using the algebraic identity (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²:

⇒ 1/x = (2 − √5) / [2² − (√5)²]

⇒ 1/x = (2 − √5) / (4 − 5)

⇒ 1/x = (2 − √5) / (−1)

⇒ 1/x = −2 + √5

⇒ 1/x = √5 − 2

Now, calculate the value of (x − 1/x):

⇒ x − 1/x = (2 + √5) − (√5 − 2)

⇒ x − 1/x = 2 + √5 − √5 + 2

⇒ x − 1/x = 4

Finally, compute the cube of the result:

⇒ (x − 1/x)³ = 4³

⇒ (x − 1/x)³ = 64

**∴ The correct answer is 64.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rationalization of Surds

To rationalize a fraction with a denominator of the form √a + √b, multiply both numerator and denominator by its conjugate √a − √b to eliminate the square root from the base.

Difference of Squares Identity

The product of the sum and difference of two terms is given by the algebraic formula: (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².

Reciprocal Shortcut for Surds

If x = √a + √b and the difference between their squares is 1 (i.e., a − b = 1), then its reciprocal can be directly written as 1/x = √a − √b.

options.text: Ratio of areas of two similar triangles = Ratio of squares of corresponding segments obtained by corresponding angle bisectors.

The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles is always equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding linear dimensions.

Linear dimensions include side lengths, altitudes, medians, perimeters, and angle bisectors.

Options 1, 2, and 3 correctly state that the area ratio equals the ratio of the squares of these corresponding lengths.

Option 4 incorrectly equates the area ratio directly to the linear segment ratio without squaring it, making it dimensionally incorrect.

**∴ The correct answer is Ratio of areas of two similar triangles = Ratio of corresponding segments obtained by corresponding angle bisectors.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Concept Used:**

⇒ When two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is strictly equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding side lengths.

⇒ Area(ΔABC) ÷ Area(ΔPQR) = (AB ÷ PQ)² = (BC ÷ QR)² = (AC ÷ PR)²

**∴ The correct answer is Ratio of areas of two similar triangles = Ratio of corresponding segments obtained by corresponding angle bisectors.**

Ratio of Perimeters in Similar Triangles

The ratio of the perimeters of two similar triangles is equal to the direct ratio of their corresponding sides (without any squaring). Perimeter represents a linear 1D measurement.

Angle Bisector Theorem

An interior angle bisector of a triangle divides the opposite side into two proportional segments that correspond to the lengths of the other two adjacent sides: BD ÷ DC = AB ÷ AC.

Similarity Criteria

Two triangles are determined to be completely similar if they satisfy the AAA (Angle-Angle-Angle), SAS (Side-Angle-Side), or SSS (Side-Side-Side) criteria. Similar triangles always maintain identical shapes but may differ in size.

questions.question: Ashok, Bharat, and Chand enter into a partnership. Ashok contributes one-third of the whole capital while Bharat contributes as much as Ashok and Chand together. If the profit at the end of the year is Rs. 96,000, how much would Chand receive? (in Rs.)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ashok contributes 1/3 of the total capital.

Bharat contributes as much as Ashok and Chand together, so his capital must be exactly half, i.e., 1/2.

Chand's capital = Total − (Ashok + Bharat) = 1 − (1/3 + 1/2) = 1/6.

Since the time period is identical, profit is distributed based on capital directly.

Chand's share = 1/6 × Total Profit = 1/6 × 96000 = 16000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹16000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total profit at the end of the year = ₹96000

Ashok's capital (A) = 1/3 of total

Bharat's capital (B) = Ashok's capital (A) + Chand's capital (C)

**Formula Used:**

Profit Ratio = Capital × Time

When time is the same for all, Profit Ratio = Capital Ratio

 
• 
 
 
 Ratio: 2
 Ashok

 
 Ratio: 3
 Bharat

 
 Ratio: 1
 Chand

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the total capital of the partnership be 1 unit.

⇒ Total Capital = A + B + C = 1

⇒ Since B = A + C, substitute (A + C) with B:

⇒ B + B = 1

⇒ 2B = 1

⇒ B = 1/2

⇒ Now, Chand's capital (C) = 1 − (A + B)

⇒ C = 1 − (1/3 + 1/2)

⇒ C = 1 − 5/6 = 1/6

⇒ Capital Ratio (A : B : C) = 1/3 : 1/2 : 1/6

⇒ Multiply the ratio by 6 (LCM of 3, 2, 6):

⇒ A : B : C = 2 : 3 : 1

⇒ Total ratio parts = 2 + 3 + 1 = 6

⇒ Chand's profit share = (1 / 6) × 96000

⇒ Chand's profit share = 16000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹16000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Partnership

When all partners invest their capital for the identical time period, the profit is distributed directly in proportion to their initial investments.

Compound Partnership

When partners invest for varying time periods, the profit is shared in the ratio of the product of their capital and duration of investment (C₁×T₁ : C₂×T₂).

Sleeping Partner

A partner who invests capital but does not actively manage the business. The working partner usually receives a specified salary or percentage of profit before the rest is distributed based on capital.

questions.question: If the mode of a data exceeds its mean by 16.2, then the mode exceeds the median by _______. (Use empirical formula to find the answer.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

From the empirical formula, the differences between Mode, Median, and Mean always follow a fixed 2 : 1 ratio.

⇒ (Mode − Median) : (Median − Mean) = 2 : 1

⇒ Total difference (Mode − Mean) = 3 parts = 16.2

⇒ 1 part = 16.2 ÷ 3 = 5.4

⇒ Mode − Median = 2 parts = 2 × 5.4 = 10.8

**∴ The correct answer is 10.8.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Mode − Mean = 16.2

**Formula Used:**

Empirical formula: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mode − Mean = 16.2

⇒ Mean = Mode − 16.2

Substituting Mean in the empirical formula:

⇒ Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × (Mode − 16.2)

⇒ Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mode + 32.4

⇒ 3 × Mode = 3 × Median + 32.4

Empirical Relationship

For a moderately skewed distribution, the relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is given by: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Mean (Average)

It is the sum of all observations divided by the total number of observations. It is highly affected by extreme values.

Median

It is the middlemost value of a sorted data set. It divides the distribution into two equal halves and is not affected by extreme outliers.

Mode

It is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. A data set may have one mode, multiple modes, or no mode at all.

questions.question: What is the remainder when 65⁹⁹ is divided by 11 ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When dividing 65 by 11, the nearest multiple of 11 is 66, which gives a negative remainder of −1.

Substitute this negative remainder into the given expression: (−1)⁹⁹.

Since 99 is an odd power, (−1)⁹⁹ = −1.

To convert the negative remainder into a positive one, add the divisor: 11 + (−1) = 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = 65⁹⁹ ÷ 11

**Concept Used:**

If an expression is of the form (ax − 1)ⁿ ÷ a, the remainder is (−1)ⁿ.

If n is an odd number, remainder is −1, which means the actual positive remainder is (a − 1).

**Calculation:**

⇒ 65⁹⁹ ÷ 11

⇒ Expressing 65 in terms of a multiple of 11: 65 = 66 − 1 = 11 × 6 − 1

⇒ (11 × 6 − 1)⁹⁹ ÷ 11

⇒ Applying the concept, the remainder depends only on the (−1) term.

⇒ Remainder = (−1)⁹⁹

⇒ Remainder = −1

⇒ As the remainder cannot be negative, we add the divisor (11) to it.

⇒ Final positive remainder = 11 − 1 = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fermat's Little Theorem

If p is a prime number and a is not divisible by p, then ap−¹ leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by p.

Wilson's Theorem

For any prime number p, the expression (p − 1)! leaves a remainder of −1 when divided by p.

Negative Remainder Concept

A negative remainder −R indicates that the number is R less than a multiple of the divisor D. The true positive remainder is calculated as D − R.
</p

questions.question: If cos θ - sin θ = 0, then (sin⁸ θ + cos⁸ θ) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given cos θ − sin θ = 0, which implies tan θ = 1.

This means the angle θ = 45°.

At θ = 45°, sin θ = 1/√2 and cos θ = 1/√2.

Substitute the values: (1/√2)⁸ + (1/√2)⁸

⇒ 1/16 + 1/16 = 2/16 = 1/8.

**∴ The correct answer is 1/8.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

cos θ − sin θ = 0

**Calculations:**

⇒ cos θ = sin θ

Squaring both sides, we get:

⇒ cos² θ = sin² θ

Using the standard trigonometric identity:

⇒ sin² θ + cos² θ = 1

Substituting cos² θ with sin² θ:

⇒ sin² θ + sin² θ = 1

⇒ 2sin² θ = 1

⇒ sin² θ = 1/2 and cos² θ = 1/2

Now, we need to find the value of (sin⁸ θ + cos⁸ θ):

⇒ (sin² θ)⁴ + (cos² θ)⁴

⇒ (1/2)⁴ + (1/2)⁴

⇒ 1/16 + 1/16

⇒ 2/16 = 1/8

**∴ The correct answer is 1/8.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 | sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 | cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1

Important Higher Power Expansions

sin⁴θ + cos⁴θ = 1 − 2sin²θ cos²θ | sin⁶θ + cos⁶θ = 1 − 3sin²θ cos²θ

Equalities at 45°

In the first quadrant, sin θ = cos θ only when θ = 45°. Similarly, tan θ = cot θ and sec θ = cosec θ are equal at θ = 45°.

questions.question: Simplify: 12(1)/(3) + 10(5)/(6) - 7(2)/(3) - 1(4)/(7)

__Shortcut Trick__

Separate the integer and fractional parts to calculate rapidly.

Integers: 12 + 10 − 7 − 1 = 14

Fractions: 1/3 + 5/6 − 2/3 − 4/7 = −1/3 + 5/6 − 4/7 = 3/6 − 4/7 = −1/14

Combine parts: 14 − 1/14 = 13 + (14/14 − 1/14) = 13 13/14

**∴ The correct answer is 13 13/14.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

12 1/3 + 10 5/6 − 7 2/3 − 1 4/7

**Calculations:**

⇒ Converting mixed fractions to improper fractions:

⇒ 37/3 + 65/6 − 23/3 − 11/7

⇒ Grouping terms with denominator 3:

⇒ (37/3 − 23/3) + 65/6 − 11/7

⇒ 14/3 + 65/6 − 11/7

⇒ Taking LCM of 3 and 6, which is 6:

⇒ (28 + 65)/6 − 11/7

⇒ 93/6 − 11/7

⇒ Simplifying the fraction:

⇒ 31/2 − 11/7

⇒ Taking LCM of 2 and 7, which is 14:

⇒ (31 × 7 − 11 × 2) / 14

⇒ (217 − 22) / 14

⇒ 195 / 14

⇒ 13 13/14

**∴ The correct answer is 13 13/14.**

**__Additional Information__**

Mixed Fractions

A mixed fraction represents the sum of a whole number and a proper fraction. It can be split into two parts for easier addition and subtraction: A B/C = A + B/C.

BODMAS Rule

It dictates the correct order of mathematical operations: Brackets, Orders, Division/Multiplication, and Addition/Subtraction. Operations of the same rank are solved from left to right.

LCM for Fractions

When adding or subtracting fractions with different denominators, always find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the denominators to create equivalent fractions.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 p.m.**

For 2D figures having the exact same given perimeter, the figure with the greater number of sides encloses a larger area.

A circle can be considered a regular polygon with an infinite number of sides.

Thus, a circle always encloses the maximum possible area for a fixed perimeter compared to any other polygon.

Since the square and the circle have equal perimeters, the circle will enclose the greater area.

**∴ The correct answer is Area of the circle > Area of the square.**

questions.question: The sum of the digits of the smallest number which, when divided by 18, 21, 25 and 39 leaves a remainder of 3 in each case is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The smallest required number N = LCM(18, 21, 25, 39) + 3

LCM(18, 21, 25, 39) = 2 × 3² × 5² × 7 × 13 = 40950

N = 40950 + 3 = 40953

Sum of digits of N = 4 + 0 + 9 + 5 + 3 = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors = 18, 21, 25, and 39

Remainder in each case = 3

**Concept Used:**

The smallest number which, when divided by a, b, c leaves a remainder r in each case is given by the formula: LCM(a, b, c) + r.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ Prime factorization of 21 = 3 × 7

⇒ Prime factorization of 25 = 5²

⇒ Prime factorization of 39 = 3 × 13

⇒ LCM = Highest powers of all prime factors = 2 × 3² × 5² × 7 × 13

⇒ LCM = 2 × 9 × 25 × 7 × 13

⇒ LCM = 50 × 9 × 91

⇒ LCM = 450 × 91 = 40950

⇒ Required number = 40950 + 3 = 40953

⇒ Sum of digits of the number = 4 + 0 + 9 + 5 + 3 = 21

**∴ The correct answer is 21.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and Remainder Rule 1

The smallest number leaving a remainder 'r' when divided by a, b, c is calculated as LCM(a, b, c) + r.

LCM and Remainder Rule 2

The smallest number leaving remainders x, y, z when divided by a, b, c respectively is LCM(a, b, c) − K, where K = (a − x) = (b − y) = (c − z).

HCF and Remainder Rule

The largest number dividing a, b, c leaving a remainder 'r' in each case is calculated as HCF(a−r, b−r, c−r).

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 9. The remainder when any number is divided by 9 is exactly equal to the remainder when its sum of digits is divided by 9.
</p

questions.question: If 1st January, 2012 was a Sunday, then on which day was the New Year celebrated in the year 2008?
questions.solution:

01.01.2012 = Sunday

In general, the day on the same date of different years in ascending order moves forward by one day.

Calculation:

2008 and 2012 both are leap years. But in the gap between 01.01.2008 and 01.01.2012, there is only one complete leap year. 

The day will move forward from 2008 to 2012 by = 4 + 1 = 5 days

Hence, New year on 2008 was = Sunday - 5 days = Tuesday

**∴ The day New Year was celebrated in the year 2008 was Tuesday.**
